eW.text:
Some adjustable variable details: 

"ChainAnimation?" determines whether or not the pull chain animation is enabled (thus explaineth the need for two sprites for a single pull chain). It can be set to either 0 (false) or 1 (true). This variable applies to all pull chain sprites. 

"MotorHum?" determines whether or not your fan makes a humming or buzzing sound when turned on. This variable can be set to either 0 (false) or 1 (true). 

"LightKitInstalled?" Determines whether or not the light kit sprites are shown. It can be set to 0 (false) or 1 (true).

eY.text: If you want, you can change the second input that says “0.003” to give your fan a faster or slower acceleration.

e!.text: This variable determines whether or not the fan makes a humming or buzzing noise when it's turned on. This can be set to either 0 or 1.

b+.text:
Be sure to change the inputs inside the “Set TargetV to” blocks in this loop based on the speeds of the fan you’re creating. 

Pro tip: If you’d like to make your fan rotate in Rotations Per Minute rather than degrees, you can add a block to the inputs of the “Set TargetV to” blocks that divides any input value by 5. Note that this only works properly if the project is running at 30 FPS.

b#.text: This code handles the actual acceleration/deceleration of the motor based on the current target speed. You should not mess with this.

cj.text: This bit of code handles the speed of the motor's acceleration based on the current target speed. If you want to, you can change the input that says “0.015” to something different to give your fan a faster or slower acceleration.

cr.text: This code and the code above it is present to fix a bug that occurs when the fan speed is in the “off” position, and the CurrentV keeps switching back and forth between two values, which causes the fan to move slightly, when it’s supposed to stay completely still. You should not mess with this.

bW.text: If the “MotorHum?” variable is set to 1 (true), you can change the selected sound in this block to change the kind of humming/buzzing sound the fan motor makes.

_I0L;Qn^Pw[Ae4`U[1Zx.text: This variable and some code that uses it aim to give the fan a more realistic deceleration. You might want to change this if you've changed the "Decreasing Value" variable to something other than it is set to now. (0.001)

e%.text: Note: if you want to change the ACTUAL decreasing velocity value, please adjust the “Decreasing Value” variable.

e(.text: ⚠️ The size of the “Fan blades” sprite cannot be changed.

e).text: Definition of a Motorset, for those who don’t know: The motor of a ceiling fan, plus any parts that are attached to it (e.g. the fan blades).

e*.text:
This sprite should be deleted or hidden if the Hugger motor housing sprite is being used. 

Also, You should change the Y position of this sprite depending on the type of motor housing you're using.

e=.text: Switch the costume of this Sprite and change the position of this sprite to so desired. Either delete this sprite, or set the "LightKitInstalled?" variable to false if you don't plan to use a light kit on your fan.

e?.text: This variable determines whether or not the pull chain animation is enabled. 0 = No, 1 = Yes.

e[.text: This variable determines whether or not the pull chain animation is enabled. It can be set to either 0 or 1. 0 = false, 1 = true.

e^.text: This variable determines whether or not the pull chain animation is enabled. It can be set to either 0 or 1. 0 = false, 1 = true.

e`.text: This variable determines whether or not the pull chain animation is enabled. This can be set to either of these 2 values: 0 (false), and 1 (for true).

e|.text:
This variable determines whether or not the pull chain animation is enabled. You can set it to either 1 or 0. 
0 = false, and 1 = true.

cQ.text: Import your desired pull chain sound to the “sounds” tab, and this block may automatically select your chain sound once imported. If not, select your imported pull chain sound of choice using this block’s drop-down menu.

cM.text: Change this depending on the delay between the first and second click of the pull chain sound you’re using.

e~.text: Either delete this sprite, or set the "LightKitInstalled?" variable to false if you don't plan to use a light kit on your fan.

fb.text: Switch the costume of this sprite and change the position of this sprite to so desired. This additional chain exists on some Canadian ceiling fans, some Casablanca models, and maybe a FEW American ceiling fans. To use the reverse pull chain, switch the costume of the Sprite variable “ReverseOption” to “Chain”.

dm.text: Import your desired pull chain sound to the “sounds” tab, and this block may automatically select your chain sound once imported. If not, select your imported pull chain sound of choice using this block’s drop-down menu.

dt.text: Change this depending on the delay between the first and second click of the pull chain sound you’re using.

dE.text: Change the input of this block to something different if you want the reverse toggle to have a different sound to it. You should not mess with any of the code above this block.

dH.text: This code determines the visibility of the reverse toggle switch sprite depending on the configuration of the "ReverseOption" sprite variable. You should not mess with this.

fc.text: The size and color of this Sprite can be changed, depending on whether or not you’re using this as a variable speed wall control, or a variable knob integrated on the fan’s switch housing.

fd.text:
Delete any light kit costumes and sprites that you aren’t using. 

IMPORTANT: The sizes of these light kits must not be changed. The default sizes of each light kit are there to make their actual size as accurate as possible if they were on a real fan.
